reasoning: resistivity depends on the length of the wire, if we cut it in half the length becomes half so resistivity also becomes half
knownLabels: Confuses resistivity with resistance
evidence: resistivity depends on the length of the wire, if we cut it in half the length becomes half so resistivity also becomes half
feedback: You are right that cutting the wire halves its length, and that changes something. But that something is the resistance (R = ρL/A), which becomes half. Resistivity ρ is a property of the material, like density, so it stays the same. Quick check: a small piece of copper and a long copper rod have the same density, and likewise the same resistivity. So the answer is A.

reasoning: in parallel all the apliances get the same current so every one works properly and none of them gets less current than the other

evidence: in parallel all the apliances get the same current so every one works properly and none of them gets less current than the other
feedback: You are right that in parallel every appliance works properly and none is starved. But the reason is equal voltage, not equal current. In parallel each branch gets the full mains voltage, and the current in each branch depends on its resistance (I = V/R), so a heater draws much more current than a bulb. Because each branch is separate, you can also switch one appliance off without affecting the others, so the answer is C.

reasoning: we see everything the right way up not upside down, so the image on the retina has to be erect. and its not on a screen so virtual

expectedMisconception: Image on the retina is upright
gotMisconception: Image on the retina is upright
evidence: we see everything the right way up not upside down, so the image on the retina has to be erect. and its not on a screen so virtual
feedback: You are right that we see things the right way up, but that is the brain's job, not the retina's. The eye lens is a convex lens, and it forms a real, inverted image on the retina, which acts as the screen. The retina is a screen of light-sensitive cells, so the image formed there is real, and the brain flips the signal so we see objects upright. Quick check: a convex lens making a real image of a distant object (like a camera lens on a film) always gives an inverted image.

reasoning: for force on a conductor we use the right hand rule, thumb is force, first finger is field and middle finger is current
knownLabels: Uses a right-hand rule for the force
expectedMisconception: Uses a right-hand rule for the force
gotMisconception: Uses a right-hand rule for the force
evidence: for force on a conductor we use the right hand rule, thumb is force, first finger is field and middle finger is current
feedback: You remembered the finger assignments correctly: thumb is force (motion), forefinger is field, middle finger is current. But that set of assignments belongs to Fleming's left-hand rule, which is used for the force on a current-carrying conductor (motor effect). The right-hand rule is for induced current in a generator, where the thumb is the motion of the conductor. Quick check: a motor turns electrical energy into motion, so use the left hand. A generator turns motion into current, so use the right hand.

reasoning: each prism makes colours out of the light, so the 2nd prism will make more colours again and the band will be even wider
knownLabels: The prism creates the colours

evidence: each prism makes colours out of the light, so the 2nd prism will make more colours again
feedback: You are right that a prism spreads white light into a band of colours. But the prism does not make the colours. White light already contains all of them, and the prism only separates them because each colour bends by a different amount. An inverted identical prism bends each colour back the other way, so the colours recombine into white light (option C). Quick check: Newton did exactly this, and the light that came out was white again, not a wider spectrum.

reasoning: angle of incidence = angle of refelction. the ray makes 30 with the mirror so it reflects at 30 also
knownLabels: Measures angles from the mirror surface
expectedMisconception: Measures angles from the mirror surface
gotMisconception: Measures angles from the mirror surface
evidence: the ray makes 30 with the mirror so it reflects at 30 also
feedback: You remembered the law correctly: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection. But both angles are measured from the normal (the line perpendicular to the mirror), not from the mirror surface. Here the ray is 30° from the mirror, so the angle of incidence = 90° - 30° = 60°, and the angle of reflection is also 60°. Quick check: a ray hitting the mirror head-on along the normal has angle of incidence 0°, even though it makes 90° with the surface.

Aur registan ya pahad ke upar bhi sky blue hi dikhta hai, jahan door-door tak samundar nahi hota.

Isliye V double hone par I = V/R double ho jata hai. Quick check: 2 Ω ke resistor par 4 V lagao toh 2 A, 8 V lagao toh 4 A. Resistance dono baar 2 Ω hi raha.

reasoning: at sunrise the light comes thru more air, and red is scattered the most so it spreads all over and reaches our eyes, thats why sun looks red
knownLabels: Red light is scattered the most
Sky is blue because it reflects the sea
expectedMisconception: Red light is scattered the most
gotMisconception: Red light is scattered the most
evidence: red is scattered the most so it spreads all over and reaches our eyes
feedback: You are right that at sunrise the light travels through more air, and that this is why the Sun looks red. But the scattering idea is the wrong way round: blue light is scattered the most, because it has a shorter wavelength, and red is scattered the least. Over the long path most of the blue is scattered out of the beam, so the red that is left goes straight to our eyes. Quick check: danger signals and traffic lights use red because it scatters least, so it can be seen from far away through fog and haze.

reasoning: glass is denser so the ray bends towards normal. the speed of light stays same only the direction changes
knownLabels: Bends away from normal in denser medium
Light's speed is the same in every medium
expectedMisconception: Light's speed is the same in every medium
gotMisconception: Light's speed is the same in every medium
evidence: the speed of light stays same only the direction changes
feedback: You are right that glass is denser, so the ray bends towards the normal. But the speed of light does not stay the same: it slows down in glass, and this change in speed is exactly why the ray bends. Quick check: if the speed really stayed the same, there would be no reason for the direction to change at all, and refractive index (n = c/v) would always be 1.

reasoning: diamond is very heavy and dense, more mass so light slows down 2.42 times inside it
knownLabels: Higher refractive index means faster light

feedback: You are right that light slows down by a factor of 2.42 in diamond, so A is correct. But the slowing is not caused by diamond being heavy or having more mass. Refractive index measures how strongly the material interacts with light (optical density), which is a different thing from mass density. Check: the refractive index of kerosene (about 1.44) is higher than that of water (1.33), yet kerosene is lighter than water and still slows light more.
